AUTHORIZING AND DrrEcTING JOHN DICKINSON, ASSISTANT SECRETARY
OF COMMERCE, TO PERFORM THE DUTIES OF THE DIRECTOR OF THE
Bureau or ForeIGN AND Domestic COMMERCE, IN CASE OF AB-
SENCE, RESIGNATION, ETC., OF THE DIRECTOR OF SAID BUREAU.

Under the authority vested in me by section 179 of the Revised Statutes (U.S.C.,
title 5, sec. 6), I hereby authorize and direct John Dickinson, Assistant Secretary of
Commerce, to perform the duties of the Director of the Bureau of Foreign and
Domestic Commerce of the Department of Commerce in case of the resignation,
absence, or sickness of the Director of said Bureau until the sickness or absence of the
incumbent shall cease or in the event of resignation until a successor shall have been

appointed.
FRANKLIN D. ROOSEVELT.

Tue Waite Hovss,
May 11, 1984.

[No. 6708]

Signed by President William H. Taft Friday, February 4, 1910

1910 CSR 112

649148Executive Order 1162 — Authorizing Reinstatement of John H. Dickinson as Inspector in Quartermaster's Department of the Army Without Regard to Civil Service Rules1910President of the United States

John H. Dickinson, formerly employed as an inspector in the Quartermaster's Department of the Army, who was dismissed more than one year ago on account of alleged irregularities which were afterwards found to be groundless, may be reinstated as an inspector without regard to the provision of the civil-service rules limiting reinstatement to one year after separation.

Wm. H. Taft.

The White House,

February 4, 1910.
